page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 4 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The server is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of strong single-core performance and weaker multi-core and memory throughput. The Geekbench single-core score of 2114.0 and text processing score of 2438.0 are strong, placing in the top 25%. However, the stress-ng single-core performance is in the bottom 10% at 787.09, and multi-core performance is weak at 3134.25. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also weak, with read speeds at 35.68 GB/sec and write speeds at 25.08 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 5.93 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is weak at 3.61 GB/sec.

Due to its shared CPU allocation, this server exhibits lower multi-core efficiency and is not suited for sustained high-compute workloads or large-scale LLM inference, as shown by the poor 7B model prompt processing speed of 14.45 tokens/sec. However, the generous 48.0 GB memory capacity offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources. It is well-suited for caching layers, memory-heavy text processing, software compilation, and lightweight database operations where high memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-core compute power.
